Live PR #535 evidence (exact HEAD c05da168545c5fa95fe300706eccaac2228fc391): after root causes 1 and 2 were fixed, hunter_merge_readiness_v2.resolve_review_authority misclassified a live, legitimate 'pending' (WAITING_FOR_REVIEWER, orchestration cycle genuinely published) verification result as a hard MALFORMED_REVIEW failure, so Hunter Merge Readiness could never reach the pending state its own sibling review_wait_state mechanism exists to produce -- an unrecoverable false failure, since no contributor push can complete a review a reviewer was never actually dispatched to perform.

Hunter failed over Codex -> Copilot -> Gemini -> Groq, where Gemini returned HTTP 503 and Groq HTTP 403.

Live PR #535 evidence (same exact HEAD): at least two Hunter Reviewer Collector runs (36340127965 and 36340195915) were dispatched for the same exact-head cycle, and the trusted orchestration status was republished with different reconcile trigger IDs for the same exact-head waiting cycle, despite ensure_collector persisting a cycle status before every dispatch -- because GitHub's combined-status read is not guaranteed read-your-write consistent, so a second, closely-spaced reconcile execution can still observe 'absent' after an earlier one already dispatched.
